title: Add RAG Odyssey playbook and lightweight tool-factory templates
author: Evelyn Park
description: Motivation: Provide an opinionated, beginner-friendly RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) learning path that combines a narrative guided playbook with runnable templates and a tiny 'tool-factory' for local tool-calling development. This PR introduces the 'RAG Odyssey' playbook (guided scenarios, checkpoints, and assertions), a compact tool-factory microlib (Node + Python examples) to scaffold tool bindings, and a browser sandbox runner to preview end-to-end flows. Goals: (1) reduce first-time-to-success for engineers learning RAG at Redwood, (2) provide small, composable templates that can be used in tutorials and workshops, (3) ship telemetry-friendly hooks and structured output linting to encourage reproducible evals. What this contains: - README-style narrative walk-through with 5 progressive scenarios (indexing, question answering, tool-calling, multi-tool orchestration, structured-output validation). - 3 runnable templates: odyssey/basic-qa (TS), odyssey/multi-tool (TS + Py), odyssey/eval-checks (assertion harness). - tool-factory microlib: lightweight scaffolding that emits TypeScript/Python stubs and a dev-time proxy for tool-calling over WS. - Browser sandbox (static site + service worker) that can run a minimal RAG session against an in-memory index for workshops. - CI job additions: docs smoke checks, example smoke CI, and a small e2e smoke that runs headless against the sandbox. Checklist: - [x] Playbook narrative and step checkpoints - [x] Templates for TS and Python with README quickstart - [x] Tool-factory microlib with generator and examples - [x] Browser sandbox + instructions to run locally - [x] CI smoke checks and docs lint - [x] Telemetry probe hooks and structured output examples Backwards compatibility: examples and docs only; no API or runtime changes. Related: linear ENG-1932 (RAG starter kit), DOCS-451 (playbook consolidation). Usage notes: see examples/rag/odyssey/README.md for step-by-step quickstart (npm/pip install, start sandbox, run smoke). The playbook includes a set of short prompt templates and a small seed corpus (~150KB) committed under examples/rag/odyssey/data/seed, intended for local demos only. Security: sample API keys in templates are placeholder strings and the browser sandbox uses an in-memory mock—no credentials committed. License: all templates fall under the repo license.
commits: 5 commits — initial playbook scaffold; add TS basic-qa template; add tool-factory microlib; add Python multi-tool example; add browser sandbox and CI; fix docs linting
review_comments: Marcus Li: Nice narrative — please add a brief section on expected token costs for the scenarios. Suggested: include rough per-scenario token estimates and one optimised config for dev runs.

Priya Narang: Tool-factory looks promising. Request: expose a switch to opt-out of the WS dev-proxy so teams can test purely server-side tool invocation. Also add a short example showing how to stub a third-party HTTP tool in Python.
Diego Ruiz: CI smoke timing is tight on the sandbox e2e, saw intermittent flakes in CI; recommend increasing timeout and adding a retry for the headless runner.
author_responses: Evelyn Park: Added per-scenario token cost estimates in docs and included an 'economy' config for low-cost dev runs.
Evelyn Park: Exposed --no-proxy flag on the generator and added a Python stub example under templates/multi-tool/python/stubs.
Evelyn Park: Increased headless-runner timeout to 30s and added a single retry in the workflow.
release_notes: Add RAG Odyssey playbook: guided quickstart, three runnable templates (TS/Py), a tiny tool-factory scaffolder, and a browser sandbox for local workshops. No runtime or API changes. Recommended for inclusion in next docs release as a community tutorial.
motivation: Lower onboarding friction for teams experimenting with RAG by providing a narrative-led, runnable learning path and small, reusable templates for tool-calling patterns.
testing_notes: Local test: npm ci && npm run start:sandbox then run examples/rag/odyssey/templates/basic-qa/run-local.sh. CI ensures smoke runs on Node 18 and Python 3.11 images.
security_notes: No real keys committed. The tool-factory generator creates placeholder secrets; docs explicitly instruct replacing with KMS-managed credentials for private deployments.
